title: Speed-Up Chooser
description: Faster code is not always better code. Each 40 ms audio frame leaves 30 ms for the audio work after a 10 ms display reserve, and the right implementation is the simplest one whose worst-case pass time fits that limit: plain Python first, then viper, then inline assembly. If even assembly is too slow, the work itself must shrink.

learningObjectives: The learner will recommend, for 6 scenarios, the simplest implementation whose worst-case pass time fits within the frame budget minus the display reserve, or state that none fits, with at least 5 of 6 correct.
prerequisites: frame budget, display reserve, worst-case pass time, viper code, inline assembly, performance trade-offs (all defined in this chapter above the block).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: In scenario 2 the fastest option was not the right one. Why?
Why does the average pass time not decide whether an option fits?
What should you do when no option fits?
commonMisconceptions: (1) The fastest implementation is always the best choice. (2) An implementation that fits on average fits the deadline. (3) Assembly is always needed for real-time audio.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all six scenarios. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
